description: Being picked up from somewhere at an unreasonable hour. Rarely dramatic, and disproportionately load-bearing.
energy_note: Small, and holding up more than it looks.

description: Waldinger's framing is social fitness: relationships need regular care in the way a body does, and decay quietly without it. Almost nobody puts it in a calendar, which is why it decays.
energy_note: It needs tending, and nobody schedules it.

description: The study is specific: it is not the number of people but whether you feel safe with any of them. People report loneliness inside crowds and inside marriages.
energy_note: A few people you can be honest with.

description: Time in the same place, or money for the journey, or a working connection. Migration, shift work and permits all quietly cost friendships, and nobody counts that as a cost.
energy_note: Proximity, which is the thing people lose first.
notes: Pairs with DIA / PSY categories across the hurdle datasets: the isolation rows there are the negative of this one.

aspect: It predicts your health at eighty
description: People most satisfied in their relationships at fifty were the healthiest at eighty, with lower rates of diabetes, arthritis and cognitive decline. This category is not soft.
energy_note: A friendship is a medical intervention.
